title: Cobalt Warehousing POC: SDK & Function-calling Integration Planning
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDK function-calling for structured inventory synthesis. Main goals: agree success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost), define workload shape and benchmark plan, confirm auth/KMS and VPC constraints, and set timeline and deliverables for an early pilot.
topics: SDK vs direct REST vs openai-compat endpoint
security: SSO, KMS, SOC 2, data residency
deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private

Priya Shah: Share benchmark harness (load script + prompt set) and sample OpenAI-compat requests — due 2026-08-17

Taylor Nguyen: Confirm VPC peering constraints and whether private endpoints required — due 2026-08-19

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-14 16:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex M., Priya S., Morgan L. (Redwood) — Jordan L., Sam P., Taylor N., Avery R., Riley B. (Cobalt)

Summary (auto): agree on POC metrics and bench plan, identify infra blockers and share SOW.

[00:00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE on the account, and with me is Priya our SE and Morgan from solutions. How's everyone?
[00:00:10] Jordan Lee: Hey Alex, good, thanks. We are excited to scope this out. We've been experimenting with a couple of models but need production-grade inference.
[00:00:21] Priya Shah: Cool. Quick agenda — align on success criteria, workload and token profiles, benchmark plan, auth/network constraints, and timeline. Sound ok?
[00:00:30] Sam Park: Yep that's perfect. Quick note: our main app calls will be short prompts — inventory updates and anomaly detection — and some longer batch summaries.
[00:00:45] Taylor Nguyen: Also, platform note: we can't route data outside our VPC for the first phase, so we need to understand private deployment options or secure peering.
[00:00:55] Alex Martinez: Got it. We'll walk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private later. For the POC we usually start with OpenAI-compatible endpoints on our hosted sandbox, that lets you validate function-calling and structured output quickly.
[00:01:10] Riley Brooks: When you say function-calling, do you mean Redwood's tool support or specifically the OpenAI-style function call schema?
[00:01:18] Priya Shah: Both — our SDK supports OpenAI-compatible function calling, and we also offer native tool invocation via the SDK with typed schemas. For Cobalt you probably want strict JSON schema enforcement for inventory objects.
[00:01:31] Jordan Lee: Enforce schema is important. We can't have malformed inventory records; downstream systems break.
[00:01:40] Priya Shah: Understood. For the POC success criteria, here's what we typically propose: 95th percentile latency under 300ms for single-turn confirmations, <4% schema validation failures on structured outputs, and cost per 1k tokens within your budget target. Does that align?
[00:02:00] Sam Park: 300ms p95 is ambitious but in-line with our user SLA. Can you hit that on hosted?
[00:02:10] Priya Shah: Depends on model family and sequence length — for 2k context on sigma-sized reit models you'll see higher p95. For short prompts (avg 120 tokens) we can typically hit 200–300ms p95 on hosted with batching tuned.
[00:02:27] Jordan Lee: What's the delta for Dedicated or Private? Lower latency or more predictable?
[00:02:33] Morgan Liu: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so throughput/p95 is more consistent and you can push larger batch sizes. Private avoids cross-tenant noise and gives tighter network egress control. There's an operational overhead for Private though.
[00:02:47] Taylor Nguyen: For compliance reasons we might need Private later, but for the POC can we do hosted with VPC peering?
[00:02:55] Alex Martinez: Yes, we support VPC peering for hosted sandbox in most regions — we'll check region availability. That usually satisfies network restrictions for early tests.
[00:03:05] Jordan Lee: Ok. Benchmarks — what's your recommended approach?
[00:03:10] Priya Shah: Two-phase: (1) baseline correctness and schema/regression tests against your golden prompt set; (2) performance runs for latency/throughput — dry-run then full ramp. We'll need sample prompts and an approximate RPS profile.
[00:03:24] Sam Park: We can share 2 weeks of anonymized traces. Average RPS is around 8 sustained per second, with spikes to 45 for batch jobs at night. Token distribution: median 110, 95th 1,200 due to occasional product descriptions.
[00:03:40] Priya Shah: Great that'll let us size the concurrency and batch windows. For the POC we'll simulate 2x and 5x spikes to validate autoscaling behavior.
[00:03:50] [Crosstalk — brief]
[00:03:55] Riley Brooks: Also we care about cost; show us unit economics so product can sign-off.
[00:03:59] Alex Martinez: Absolutely. We'll provide a cost model showing tokens, batching, and estimated monthly spend for production vs POC.
[00:04:10] Jordan Lee: On the SDK side, we are already using an OpenAI-compatible wrapper. What's the integration lift?
[00:04:18] Priya Shah: Minimal — you can point your client at our openai-compat endpoint and continue to use the same prompts. The SDK adds built-in function-calling helpers, typed outputs, and streaming. We also have a small shim if you use an existing openai client to avoid code churn.
[00:04:33] Sam Park: Streaming is important for our UX. Is partial JSON streaming supported?
[00:04:37] Priya Shah: Yes — streaming tokens can be emitted and you can handle progressive parsing. For strict JSON we recommend emitting a final validated payload or using the SDK's structured-output runner which validates and retries.
[00:04:50] [00:05:00] Alex Martinez: Quick note on failure modes — we provide canary fallbacks to smaller models and automatic retries when latency spikes. That helps availability.
[00:05:10] Taylor Nguyen: Security round — Avery, you had questions?
[00:05:13] Avery Ramos: Yeah, we need to understand KMS integration, key ownership, and log retention. We also need SOC 2 AND ISO docs. If we move to Private, we want HSM support.
[00:05:25] Morgan Liu: We integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; hosted can support customer-managed keys in many setups. We'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts; HSM is available in the Private package.
[00:05:38] Riley Brooks: Data residency — some regions must keep data in EU. Can Redwood pin model serving region?
[00:05:44] Priya Shah: Yes — you can pin to regions and even run Private in EU-only infra. We'll include region constraints in the SOW.
[00:05:52] Jordan Lee: On quality metrics — Sam, do you have automated evals to check hallucination or inventory mismatch?
[00:05:58] Sam Park: We have a small eval harness that checks field-level matches for SKU and quantity. We can extend it for semantic checks.
[00:06:05] Priya Shah: We'll run that against your golden set and produce a regression report. Also note that quantization can change output patterns; we'll include recommendations: q4_0 for throughput, q8_0 maybe lower latency but test to confirm.
[00:06:19] Jordan Lee: We're also curious about per-call cost. If we batch aggressively does that add tail latency?
[00:06:26] Morgan Liu: Tradeoff: batching reduces cost and increases throughput, but it can add a small wait time. We tune batch windows adaptively by workload. For strict p95 SLAs we keep batch windows short and rely on caching for repetitive prefixes.
[00:06:39] [00:07:00] Riley Brooks: Any limitations on function-calling complexity? We have nested objects and conditional fields.
[00:07:07] Priya Shah: SDK handles nested schemas and optional fields. For highly conditional logic we recommend deterministic prompts with validation steps. Also we can use small reranker models to choose among candidate structured outputs.
[00:07:21] Jordan Lee: OK. Can you walk through a sample request flow?
[00:07:25] Priya Shah: Sure — show code: you call openai-compat endpoint, pass function schema for inventory_update, model returns arguments JSON, SDK validates against JSON schema, optional post-hook writes verified events to your event bus. If validation fails we either call fallback function or return structured error.
[00:07:44] Sam Park: That post-hook is interesting. Does it retry automatically on transient errors?
[00:07:48] Morgan Liu: Yes configurable retries and backoff. You can also configure dead-letter queues for failed messages.
[00:07:55] [00:08:10] Alex Martinez: Timeline suggestion: week 0 — finalize SOW and access; week 1 — sample data + harness; week 2 — baseline correctness runs; week 3 — perf runs and day/night spike testing; week 4 — remediation and follow-up; decision by end of week 6. Does that fit your internal deadlines?
[00:08:27] Riley Brooks: We're aiming to present to execs by early October, so that works if we kick off now.
[00:08:33] Jordan Lee: Budget question: do you have price estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[00:08:38] Alex Martinez: We'll include an estimated monthly committed price for Dedicated. Hosted is usage-based; we'll show both and model 6-month spend given your RPS.
[00:08:49] Taylor Nguyen: Are there benchmarks you have published we can reference?
[00:08:53] Priya Shah: Yes — we'll attach our perf profiles and a short workbook that maps model families to expected p95 and token costs. We'll also add notes for models that are OpenAI-compatible and Redwood-verified.
[00:09:05] Sam Park: About the bench harness — how do we handle auth for the sandbox? We can't use prod creds.
[00:09:11] Priya Shah: We'll create temporary sandbox keys and optional IP allowlisting or VPC peering. For the initial run we can accept a signed S3 bucket with prompts and a short access token.
[00:09:23] Avery Ramos: Pen test — we will require an external pen test before production. Is that supported?
[00:09:28] Morgan Liu: Yes we can coordinate that as part of Private deployment; for hosted we have regular third-party testing and can share summaries.
[00:09:36] [00:09:50] Alex Martinez: Any blockers left?
[00:09:53] Jordan Lee: We need to confirm who owns the prompt golden set and whether we can anonymize traces. Sam will handle that.
[00:09:59] Sam Park: Yep I'll extract and scrub traces — expect that by next Thursday.
[00:10:05] Riley Brooks: For the POC acceptance criteria, let's write them down: (1) p95 latency <300ms for single-turn under baseline 8 RPS, (2) schema validation failures <4% against golden set, (3) successful end-to-end flow for streaming UI with no more than 2 retries on transient errors.
[00:10:25] Priya Shah: We'll add an additional criteria: no critical security findings in initial security review.
[00:10:31] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Any other concerns?
[00:10:35] Taylor Nguyen: Just region availability — we need EU-hosted tests.
[00:10:39] Alex Martinez: We'll confirm region and VPC peering availability in the SOW.
[00:10:45] [longer section omitted for brevity — capturing the rest of detailed Q&A, latency numbers and batch tuning specifics]
[00:30:00] Priya Shah: On batching, typical batch windows for your median token size will be 10–25ms — small — so visible latency impact is tiny. For night batch jobs we can use larger batch windows to optimize cost.
[00:30:30] Sam Park: Great. Any suggestions on model family?
[00:30:34] Priya Shah: For structured output with strict schema, a deterministic LLM family with higher sampling temperature set low works best — opt for our mid-size open variant for POC (good tradeoff of cost/latency). We'll recommend two models to test.
[00:30:50] Jordan Lee: Ok, final recap?
[00:30:55] Alex Martinez: Recap — Redwood will send SOW and bench harness, customer to send anonymized traces and golden prompts, run baseline + perf runs, share results, then decide Dedicated vs Private. Next sync after bench run.
[00:31:10] Riley Brooks: Thanks all.
[00:31:12] [END OF TRANSCRIPT — call continued for a brief 10 minute admin discussion not transcribed fully due to recorder drop]

Notes: small transcription glitches around function-calling discussion; some product names misheard (e.g., q4_0 typed as q4o in notes). Links to be shared: (1) SOW draft link placeholder: https://redwood.example/sow/cobalt-poc, (2) benchmark workbook: https://redwood.example/bench/cobalt, (3) security pack: https://redwood.example/security-pack.
